thread:
sam_acme: Hey all — noticed our Daily Usage chart in Console splits traffic for June 3 around 23:00 local time. Our org tz is America/Los_Angeles and finance is seeing duplicated rows in the CSV export.

maria-support: Sorry about the trouble. Can you paste your org id and one exported CSV sample? :mag:

sam_acme: org_id=acme-42. Uploaded sample to shared bucket: https://files.example/acme-usage-jun3.csv — you can see events at 2026-06-03T23:58:xx that ended up on 2026-06-04 in the export.

maria-support: I can repro in support view. Console chart also shows a cutoff at 00:00 UTC instead of 00:00 PDT. Escalating to eng. @devon-eng tagging you for triage.

devon-eng: Thanks. Quick clarifying q: is this only the chart render or are back-end aggregates using UTC buckets too?

sam_acme: Both. The aggregated CSV uses day buckets that appear to be UTC-based which caused their June 3 totals to split and sum incorrectly.

devon-eng: Reproduced locally by setting org timezone to America/Los_Angeles and loading Billing -> Daily usage. The bucket boundary is at midnight UTC. Initial hunch: windowing / bucket computation forcing UTC. Pushing to SRE to check ingestion/stream job configs. @lee-sre any findings?

lee-sre: Confirmed. The usage-aggregator-v3 streaming job introduced in the Feb deploy defaulted to UTC windowing. Code snippet: 

```
val bucketDate = Instant.ofEpochMilli(eventTs).atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate()
```

This forces all bucket keys to UTC local dates.

maria-support: That would explain it — non-UTC orgs see shifts near midnight. Can we offer a short-term mitigation? Customers are already escalated.

lee-sre: Short-term mitigation options:
1) Frontend/render-time shift: apply org timezone offset when displaying chart tiles and when generating CSVs at request time. Fast to ship, no re-agg of historical data.
2) Backfill/re-agg: change aggregator to compute bucket keys using org timezone (lookup on record) and run a re-aggregation job to rebuild historical rows. Accurate but heavy (24+ hours for backfill, schema risk).

devon-eng: I'll draft a change to compute bucketDate using the org's tz mapping and add a compatibility layer so reads can remap older rows if needed. That's ENG-9573. But it needs a safe migration plan.

maria-support: Customer asked for ETA. Is a frontend/export rendering fix feasible this week?

lee-sre: Yes — we can implement a render-time timezone-aware label and CSV generator that uses org timezone by Friday EOD PST. Note: it won't retroactively modify any CSVs already sent to customers.

devon-eng: For the backend fix, we need to decide whether to: (A) re-bucket all events by org tz at aggregation time and write new rows (re-agg), or (B) keep UTC buckets and apply read-time remap for "legacy" data. Both have trade-offs. I'll outline them in ENG-9573 and target the backend change for next sprint pending approval.

maria-support: I'll let the customer know we can ship a display/export mitigation this week and follow up with a plan for correcting historical aggregates. Sam, is that OK?

sam_acme: That timeline is acceptable. Can you also provide a short explanation we can share with our finance team about why June 3 had duplicates?

maria-support: Draft note to share: "Root cause: internal daily aggregation used UTC day boundaries; your org is configured to America/Los_Angeles. Events occurring near local midnight were assigned to different UTC dates, causing split totals in charts and exports. Temporary mitigation: Console and new CSV exports will respect your org timezone at render time starting this week. Permanent fix: we plan to adjust aggregation bucket keys and/or run a re-aggregation to align historical data in a follow-up release." Feel free to tweak.

devon-eng: Filed ENG-9573 (agg timezone fix + backfill plan). I've attached repro steps, logs from usage-aggregator-v3, and the snippet showing UTC bucketing.

metrics-bot: Alert created: ENG-9573 -> "usage aggregator timezone bucket mismatch". Owners assigned.

maria-support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with the mitigation ETA and close the loop when the render/export change is live. :thumbsup:
